Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The snapshot looks like early 2010, with unemployment at 9.4% and the fed funds rate near 0.17%.

Unemployment of 9.4% with a falling 3-month change (-0.2) suggests the rate peaked around 10.0% in October 2009 and had eased to about 9.7% by early 2010. A 9.4% reading would fit better in mid-2010 or later, but then the 12m change would be -0.5, meaning a year earlier it was 9.9%. That doesn't fit 2010, since the rate was about 9.5% in mid-2009. It fits December 2010 better: the rate was 9.4% then, versus 9.9% in December 2009 (about -0.5), and 9.8% in September 2010 (-0.4 over 3 months, close to the -0.2 shown).

Other readings fit December 2010 as well:
- The 10-year yield was about 3.36% at the end of December 2010, up from about 2.5% in September, a rise of roughly 0.73 over 3 months.
- Headline CPI was 1.5% year on year, and core CPI was 0.8%, close to the figures shown.
- The S&P 500 gained about 6.7% in December and 10.8% in the quarter, which is a little higher than shown, but the pattern is similar.
- Gold fell in December 2010 after its earlier rally, which matches the -5.2% 1-month return (the month shows a drop in early December and a partial recovery).
- The VIX ended 2010 near 17.5, a bit under the 20.04 shown.

Industrial production was up about 5.9% year on year in late 2010, which fits. Equities may not match exactly, but November 2010 fits less well: the 10-year yield was about 2.8% then. I'm going with December 2010 for the overall fit.
